short: A comprehensive economic and constitutional overhaul by the Athenian statesman Solon, establishing the foundation for Athenian democracy.
full:
Facing severe economic inequality and the threat of civil war, Athenians granted Solon exceptional powers to reform the state. He immediately instituted the seisachtheia (the "shaking off of burdens"), cancelling all debts and prohibiting the practice of debt slavery, which freed many impoverished citizens and prevented an agrarian crisis.

Constitutionally, Solon broke the exclusive aristocratic monopoly on power by organizing citizens into four property classes, tying political rights to wealth rather than birth. He established a new Council of Four Hundred and broadened the role of the popular assembly, laying a moderate but vital groundwork that later allowed radical democracy to flourish.
